bullets.title: May CPI in line; core softer at 0.2% vs 0.3% est—inflation narrative mixed
bullets.body: May CPI came in at 4.2% YoY as expected, with headline MoM at 0.5% matching estimates. The notable beat came from core CPI at +0.2% MoM vs +0.3% consensus, driven by an unexpected 1.7% plunge in car insurance—the largest drop since COVID. Ex-insurance, core would have printed hotter. JPMorgan sees May as a 'high-water mark.' PPI was hotter: headline +1.1% MoM vs +0.7% est, with final demand goods surging +2.8%—the largest monthly jump on record.

bullets.title: Iran deal nears; Strait of Hormuz reopening within 30 days under US-Iran MOU
bullets.body: A US-Iran MOU reportedly stipulates Hormuz reopening within 30 days, with US forces withdrawing from areas surrounding Iran. Options markets shifted from put-skewed to call-bid; Brent fell 4-5% on deal news. Iran's Mehr News claims the agreement includes $24B in funds, sanction relief, and Iranian asset unfreezing, though Tehran emphasizes no commitment on Hormuz management.

bullets.title: Mag 7 premarket rebound Jun 12; SpaceX IPO begins trading at $138/share (4x oversubscribed)
bullets.body: Mag 7 stocks all opened higher Friday: Alphabet +1.3%, Meta +1%, Amazon +1%, with NVDA, MSFT, TSLA and AAPL each gaining 0.4-0.7%. SpaceX's $75B IPO priced at $135, opened at $138 (+2.2%), with gray-market data having priced in a 30-35% pop. The probability of a 20%+ first-day gain surged to 62% (from 20%) and 30%+ to 46%.

bullets.title: Nasdaq-100 rebalancing: NBIS, CRWV, ALAB added; CHTR removed
bullets.body: The Nasdaq-100 is rebalancing to add Nebius (NBIS), CoreWeave (CRWV), and Astera Labs (ALAB), while Charter Communications (CHTR) is removed. SOXL alone generated ~$12B in net rebalancing demand—roughly 45% of its prior-day AUM—highlighting levered ETFs' structural market impact.

bullets.title: Oracle ORCL: $40B capital raise warning triggers 11%+ selloff; AI backlog surges to $638B
bullets.body: ORCL dropped 11%+ after announcing plans to raise ~$40B in debt and equity in FY2027 for AI data center buildout. Despite negative FY2026 FCF of -$23.7B, Oracle's AI backlog surged to $638B (4.6x YoY), signed $67B of AI infrastructure contracts in Q4, and guided FY27 capex to $90-95B. HSBC cut PT to $316 from $345; Cramer recommended buying the dip.

bullets.title: NVDA: CEO denies 800V/CPO delays; new GPU, CPU, and AI infrastructure wins
bullets.body: NVDA's networking SVP denied SemiAnalysis reports of 800V DC and CPO delays, with Morgan Stanley's Computex checks corroborating no pushback. NVDA is also: pivoting Vera CPUs for China sales (pre-orders potentially August), pursuing 10GW Ohio data center with OpenAI backing, launching a healthcare AI model with Abridge, and driving 14% of S&P 500's single-day move. Lumentum CEO separately confirmed CPO ramp on schedule for H2 2027/2028 formal ramp.

bullets.title: ECB hikes 25bps to 2.25%—first increase since 2023—amid Iran war energy shock
bullets.body: The ECB raised all three key rates by 25bps (deposit to 2.25%, refi to 2.40%), its first hike since 2023, citing persistent energy-driven inflation. ECB raised 2026 inflation forecast to 3.0% from 2.6% and cut 2026 GDP to 0.8% from 0.9%. Lagarde called the decision unanimous and signaled no pre-set rate path, but indicated further hikes possible in September if energy stays elevated.

bullets.title: Citi double-upgrades AMD to Buy with $575 PT; BofA raises 2030 server CPU TAM to $170B
bullets.body: Citi upgraded AMD from Hold to Buy, raising PT to $575 from $460, citing agentic AI demand tailwinds. BofA separately lifted its 2030 server CPU TAM forecast to $170B from $125B (+36%), citing agentic AI as a major demand driver. AMD marketing chief also boasted '15 of 15' Amazon best-seller CPU spots, locking Intel out entirely.

bullets.title: TSMC record May revenue NT$417B (+30.1% YoY); Jan-May exports +58% as AI demand accelerates
bullets.body: TSMC reported record May revenue of NT$417B (+30.1% YoY, +1.5% MoM), tracking above Q2 guidance midpoint. Taiwan's semiconductor exports rose 58.3% YoY in May to $25.5B, comprising 32.5% of all exports. TSMC also accelerated CoPoS advanced packaging timeline from 2029 to 2028.

bullets.title: META faces EU antitrust order: must give rival AI chatbots free WhatsApp access within 5 days
bullets.body: EU antitrust regulators ordered META to grant competing AI chatbots unrestricted access to WhatsApp at no cost. META called the order 'excessive regulation funded by European companies' and announced plans to challenge it legally. META must comply within five days or face regulatory consequences; the EU says the order stands until investigation is complete.

bullets.title: PLTR CEO Karp calls out AI cost-cutting hype; Baird reiterates $200 PT after AIPCon 10
bullets.body: Palantir CEO Alex Karp warned executives against using AI as pretext for mass layoffs, describing such claims as lacking substance. Separately, Baird reiterated Outperform on PLTR with a $200 PT after attending AIPCon 10, identifying five underappreciated investor points. Karp also expressed bullishness on SpaceX 'if the person doing it knows what they're doing.'

bullets.title: OpenAI in talks for 10GW Ohio data center; Nvidia exploring financial backing
bullets.body: OpenAI is in advanced negotiations to lease a proposed 10-gigawatt data center campus on federal land in Ohio, with SoftBank to build the facility and Nvidia potentially providing financial backing. Separately, Sam Altman told employees OpenAI expects to go public 'within the next year,' with a tender offer planned 'very soon' at $687.69/share.

bullets.title: Dan Ives flags AI market dynamics shifting: PLTR, SNOW, CRM positioned to thrive
bullets.body: Dan Ives (Wedbush) flagged shifting AI market dynamics where PLTR, SNOW, and CRM are positioned to be the primary beneficiaries, per a Business Insider retweet circulated on fintwit. The theme aligns with broader commentary about the AI market moving from infrastructure spending to enterprise software adoption.

bullets.title: Korea semiconductor supply chain: SK Hynix ADR listing by August; export semiconductor surge 206%
bullets.body: SK Hynix reportedly chose Nasdaq for a US listing (potentially completing by mid-August); South Korea's June 1-10 semiconductor exports surged 206% YoY to a record $28.6B total. SK Hynix also plans to triple wafer capacity by 2034. A chemical exposure incident at the Cheongju site sent two to hospital.

bullets.title: China Japan semiconductor supply chain risk: tungsten/WF6 export controls threaten TSM, Samsung, SK Hynix
bullets.body: China's export controls on tungsten (WF6) disrupted Japan's semiconductor gas supply chain, affecting TSMC, Samsung, and SK Hynix chipmakers. U.S. officials have pressed China multiple times to resolve InP (indium phosphide) export approval delays, which are creating difficulties for photonic chip manufacturers. A Reuters report confirmed China's InP controls threaten AI datacenter buildout.

bullets.title: SMCI: $7B equity shelf filing; $39B AI server order claims questioned
bullets.body: Super Micro Computer filed a $7B mixed securities shelf offering, triggering a 15-25% intraday drop. Earlier reports claimed SMCI received $39B in AI server orders in recent weeks—but the tweet author questioned whether orders flowed through an SPV. The capital raise signals ongoing investment needs.

bullets.title: Net equity supply turns positive for first time since pandemic; BofA sees $700B+ IPO supply wave in 2026
bullets.body: Net equity supply has shifted positive for the first time since the pandemic began, per fintwit commentary. Equity supply from IPOs and lockup expirations is on pace to hit a record $700B+ in 2026. IPO activity surge is historically associated with weaker forward S&P 500 returns, per BCA Research.

bullets.title: Google TPU on Samsung 2nm and NVDA confidential compute powering Apple PCC
bullets.body: Reports indicate Google is considering using Samsung Foundry's 2nm process for TPU v10 I/O die production—a potential shift away from TSMC for advanced chip manufacturing. Separately, NVIDIA's Confidential Computing GPUs are now powering Apple's Private Cloud Compute, with Apple Intelligence workloads expanding to Google Cloud via Nvidia infrastructure.

bullets.title: ORCL AAPL MSFT AMZN premarket moves Jun 11; big-tech hyperscaler capex debt issuance up 47%
bullets.body: Premarket on Jun 11 showed Tesla +1%, NVDA +0.7%, Amazon +0.5%, Meta +0.2%, Alphabet +0.2%, Apple +0.4%, MSFT flat. AI hyperscalers (GOOGL, AMZN, META, MSFT, ORCL) issued $159B in debt in the first 5 months of 2026—47% more than all of 2024. MSFT also restricted Claude Fable for employees citing data retention concerns, while an Xbox restructuring with major layoffs was announced.

bullets.title: LITE confirms CPO ramp on schedule for H2 2027; NPO opportunity 'frankly bigger than CPO'
bullets.body: Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston confirmed at both Needham and Mizuho conferences that LITE is on pace to meet or exceed Q guidance top-end, NVDA scale-out and scale-up CPO timelines remain on track, and the NPO opportunity could be larger than CPO. The CEO appeared for two consecutive conference days. SemiAnalysis reports that CPO was delayed were disputed by FundaAI and NVDA itself.
